subject: Re: MAP & Billing / PO requirements for evaluation -> production
thread_text:
From: Caroline Park <c.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Subject: Evaluation plan & procurement questions

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Platform looks promising. Before we commit engineering time to a 30-day evaluation, procurement and security asked for clarity on:

- A mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and sign-offs (security review, pilot acceptance, production ramp).
- Commercial milestones tied to pricing/commits (we need visibility into staged discounts if we scale).
- Payment terms and PO timing — Acme typically runs Net60 for new vendors and will issue a PO before the billing start date.

Can you share a MAP + sample commercial terms and confirm whether Redwood can accept Net60 and invoice monthly? Also, our legal needs to see who signs the SOW and whether billing can start after acceptance testing.

Appreciate a concise doc we can push to procurement.

— Caroline
Caroline Park
Director, Platform Operations
Acme Health

On Tue, 10 Mar 2026 at 11:03 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
To: Caroline Park <c.park@acmehealth.com>
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & procurement questions

Hi Caroline —

Great questions. I put together a short MAP and commercial note that addresses the items procurement usually asks for. High level:

MAP (example timeline)
- Week 0: PO / procurement paperwork in flight; security questionnaire delivered by Redwood (we can start SOC2 artifacts in parallel).
- Weeks 1–4: 30-day evaluation (pilot) — up to 100k tokens/day included in pilot quota.
- Week 5: Pilot acceptance (engineering sign-off on latency/accuracy thresholds).
- Weeks 6–12: Production ramp (phased ramp to committed capacity).

Commercial callouts
- Pilot pricing: free evaluation quota; additional pilot usage billed at a reduced eval rate (see attached quote).
- Commit options: 12-month commit at $120k/year for baseline tier (example). 6-month ramp discounts available at milestone sign-off (5% after pilot acceptance, additional 5% at 6-month committed usage).
- Payment terms: Standard Redwood policy is Net30. We can consider Net60 for enterprise with an administrative fee or contract credit terms to protect cash flow.
- Invoicing cadence: Monthly invoices are standard; we can align first invoice to billing start date (post-acceptance) if procurement requires it.

I'll loop in Sales Ops to confirm what concessions we can offer on Net60 and who owns the signature blocks on the SOW. Attaching MAP and quote now.

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-AcmeHealth-v1.pdf (MAP + milestones), quote-ACME-2026-03-14.pdf (line-item pricing)

Best,
Ben Carter

Subject: Fwd: MAP & Billing / PO requirements for evaluation -> production

Marissa / Dev —

Forwarding Acme's note and my proposed MAP / commercial summary (attached). They specifically asked whether we can accept Net60 and require the PO to be issued before billing start. They also want billing to start after acceptance testing (pilot acceptance).

What flexibility do we have on:
1) Accepting Net60 without adding a fee (they're a mid-sized healthcare org; may be strategic).
2) Offering the staged discounts tied to MAP milestones (pilot acceptance + 6-month ramp).
3) SOW signature — can we bill only after acceptance? Legal prefers an explicit billing start clause.

Can you weigh in quickly so I can give a firm answer?

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP & Billing / PO requirements for evaluation -> production

Ben —

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers:
- Net60: We can accept Net60 for strategic healthcare customers, finance will want advance visibility (HubSpot deal must show forecasted AR), but we shouldn't add a fee as a default. We can ask for a signed SOW + PO in advance of the first invoice.
- Milestone discounts: Approved in principle. We should structure as conditional credits applied to the next invoice rather than retroactive refunds (simpler operationally).
- Billing start date: Legal is okay with billing starting post-acceptance. Include an acceptance criteria section in the SOW (latency SLA + feature list) and state billing begins on the date of customer acceptance sign-off or 14 days after pilot end if no response.

Dev — can you draft the invoice cadence language and update the quote to show:
  a) Monthly invoicing;
  b) Billing start equals "Acceptance Date" (defined in SOW);
  c) PO required prior to first invoice;
  d) Milestone credits applied on next invoice after milestone approval.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:18:00 -0700

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: MAP & Billing / PO requirements for evaluation -> production

Caroline —

Thanks for the clarity. Per our internal review we can accommodate Acme's procurement needs with the following commercial and operational terms (summary below; full MAP & SOW attached):

Summary of agreed terms (proposal)
- MAP: 30-day pilot (Weeks 1–4) with acceptance criteria documented in the attached SOW. Production ramp to follow Weeks 6–12.
- Pricing / commits: Example 12-month committed tier = $120k/year. Milestone credits: 5% credit applied after pilot acceptance; additional 5% credit applied once monthly committed usage >= agreed baseline for two consecutive months. Credits applied to next invoice as a line-item adjustment.
- Payment terms: Redwood will accept Net60 for this engagement. No additional administrative fee.
- Invoicing cadence: Monthly invoices.
- PO requirements: Acme to provide a PO before Redwood issues the first invoice.
- Billing start date: Billing starts on the "Acceptance Date" defined in the SOW (customer sign-off). If acceptance sign-off is not returned within 14 days of pilot completion, billing will start automatically on day 15.

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-AcmeHealth-v1.pdf, quote-ACME-2026-03-14.pdf, SOW-proposed.xlsx

Next steps
1) Please confirm PO timing (can procurement commit to issuing the PO within two weeks of pilot kickoff?).
2) If Net60 needs additional internal approvals on your side, tell me the contact on procurement and I will loop in Revenue Ops to expedite.
3) If the acceptance criteria need tweaks, point us to specific items in the SOW and we'll update.

We're aiming to get the PO and SOW signed so the pilot can start the week of Mar 22 if that aligns with your team.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0189

- Acme can accept the proposed approach and will issue a PO. Procurement estimates PO issuance two business weeks after receipt of the final SOW (so roughly by Apr 1 if we sign this week).

- Invoice cadence monthly is fine; procurement requests all invoices to reference the PO number and the SOW line items for faster reconciliation.
- Billing start: procurement will accept billing starting on the Acceptance Date per SOW. We'll aim to sign acceptance within the 14-day window, but please include the automatic billing fallback language as you suggested.

Next actions from Acme side:
1) Procurement will wait for the final SOW and submit PO once received. (procure@acmehealth.com)
2) Security will run the SOC2 questionnaire in parallel — expect a follow-up from security@acmehealth.com.

If you can send the final SOW with the acceptance clause and PO instructions by end of day Mon, Mar 16, we'll try to keep the PO timeline intact.

Caroline
